newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: DCC aims to develop existing business.
newsitem.headline: DCC aims to develop existing business.

text.p: Irish industrial holding group DCC Plc said on Tuesday that its primary emphasis remained on the growth and development of its existing business and it had no plans to get into any new industry sectors.
The group is currently focused in four areas -- food, energy, healthcare and computers.
Chief executive Jim Flavin said DCC was seeking to grow internationally in the healthcare and computer sectors but was happy to develop its food and energy business closer to home.
The group hopes to build on its leading niche market positions within Ireland in the food division.
In the energy section, the emphasis will be on organic growth, cash generation and cost control, Flaving said.

In the computer division, DCC plans to continue to develop its distribution businesses in Britain and Ireland both organically and by acquisition and is considering European acquisitions. It also hopes to broaden the range of manufacturing services.
The computer division reported a drop of 21.5 percent in first half operating profit to 2.74 million Irish pounds while margins declined to 3.4 percent from 4.9 percent.

But Flavin said the downturn had been anticipated and the results were ahead of budget. He said the division had a poor first half in manual printing but this now accounted for less than 25 percent of profits and should not have the same impact in the second half.
"We feel very good about the outlook for that division in the second half. We would anticipate strong profit growth," he said.
Flavin said DCC saw healthcare as a growth area given demographic trends and is targeting mobility and rehabilitation products as a specific focus for its development.
The division reported an operating profit of 2.89 million Irish pounds in the six months to September 30, a rise of 194 percent.
"It's a relatively fragmented industry internationally and one we are determined to build an international business in," he told a news conference.
Earlier, DCC reported a 54 percent rise in half-year pre-tax profit to 15.75 million Irish pounds and said the outlook for the second half was good.
"Overall, we feel good. The first bit of the second half has started in a good way," Flavin said.
